epochs.name: Tridentine & Spanish Habsburg Era
epochs.note: Council of Trent mandates parish baptismal and marriage registers across Italy; Spanish Habsburg Viceroyalties govern Naples, Sicily, Sardinia, and Milan alongside Venice, Genoa, Tuscany, Savoy, and the Papal States.

epochs.name: 18th-Century Dynastic Realignments & Pre-Napoleonic Censuses
epochs.note: Savoy becomes Kingdom of Sardinia (1720); Bourbon dynasty establishes independent Kingdom of Naples & Sicily (1734) and compiles the 1741 Catasto Onciario; Austrian Habsburgs compile the Catasto Teresiano in Lombardy (1760); Habsburg-Lorraine governs Tuscany (1737).

epochs.name: Pre-Napoleonic transition
epochs.note: Parish registers. The old states are still the frame, under revolutionary pressure.

epochs.name: Napoleonic era
epochs.note: Stato Civile Napoleonico spreads through the Kingdom of Italy, the French departments, and Murat's Naples. Sicily and the island of Sardinia stay outside it.

epochs.name: Restoration
epochs.note: Two Sicilies, Lombardy–Venetia, the Papal States, Tuscany, Sardinia, Parma, and Modena.

epochs.name: Unification
epochs.note: The Kingdom of Italy is proclaimed on 17 March 1861. Veneto, Mantua, Rome, and the Austrian south Tyrol are still outside.

epochs.name: Civil code of 1866
epochs.note: Stato Civile Italiano starts on 1 January 1866. Veneto and Mantua are annexed in October 1866. Their civil series starts on 1 September 1871.

epochs.name: Rome in the Kingdom
epochs.note: Rome is taken on 20 September 1870. Lazio civil registration starts in 1871. The Austrian frontier still runs above Verona and east of Udine.

epochs.name: Annexations and the later Kingdom
epochs.note: Trentino, Alto Adige, Trieste, Gorizia, Istria, and Zara enter the Kingdom. The 1920s bring comuni soppressi, renames, and new provinces.

epochs.name: Italian Republic
epochs.note: The 1947 eastern border, then the modern province splits.

records.name: Registri parrocchiali
records.note: Baptisms, marriages, and burials, plus Stati delle Anime where they survive.

records.name: Stato Civile Napoleonico
records.note: Civil births, marriages, and deaths introduced under French or Napoleonic rule.

records.name: Stato Civile Borbonico
records.note: Mainland South from 1809. Sicily from 1 January 1820. The Bourbons kept the series after 1815.

records.name: Stato Civile del Granducato di Toscana
records.note: From 1817, usually kept as a duplicate of the parish register.

records.name: Stato Civile sabaudo
records.note: From 1838 in the Kingdom of Sardinia. Priests often kept the register.

records.name: Matriken austriaci
records.note: In Austrian and Austro-Hungarian lands the parish Matriken were the legal register.

records.name: Stato Civile Italiano
records.note: The national series. The start year depends on when this town entered the system.

records.name: Fuori dallo Stato italiano
records.note: This ground is not an Italian comune on this date.
